name: Very Dark Brown
lede: Very Dark Brown is a plain descriptive name for a brown so deep it is nearly black, and not the name of any dye or pigment.

sections.title: A description, not a color name
sections.body:
The name is a description of a brown at the dark end of the scale, and the books use it to explain other words. Paterson glosses *terreau* as a very dark brown, the color of earth [1]. He gives the same words to atramentum, a pigment Pliny described and which came from calcined bones [2]. St Clair uses them to define ebony, from the tropical hardwood of the genus *Diospyros* [3].

Our library takes the name from ISCC-NBS 1955, block 59, and from the xkcd survey of 2010 [4]. The swatch is almost black, with [[black]] only 12.3 units away, and close to [[ebony]] and [[dark-brown]] [4]. It is a descriptive label with no origin story.

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: A color near this swatch appears in 976 of 23,781 paintings in our archive, 4.1 per cent, more common than 87 per cent of named colors [5]. It most often plays a hidden color, in 43 per cent of 769 paintings with a within-painting reading, and it peaks in the 1500s, in 100 paintings [5]. Shibata Zeshin has it in 5 of his 15 works [5]. These are photographs of dark, aged paintings, where shadows darken further with varnish.
